summary: On 26 February 2026 an AI coding agent running Terraform destroyed the production infrastructure of the DataTalks.Club course platform, including its database and automated snapshots. The Terraform state file was on an old laptop and an older state file was swapped in. AWS Support restored a snapshot about 24 hours later. This file uses secondary reports of the author's account.

overview.background: Alexey Grigorev used Claude Code to move a site to AWS, reusing the Terraform configuration of his course platform, so both shared one VPC. The Terraform state file stayed on his previous computer.
systems: An AI coding agent given Terraform access
VPC, RDS, ECS cluster, load balancers and a bastion host
overview.impact: The platform was down for about a day. The restored courses_answer table had 1,943,200 rows according to one report.
overview.severity: Severe for a small platform, with data restored after AWS Business Support intervened.
overview.gaps: The author's post (the card source) could not be fetched. This file uses two secondary reports, which may differ in detail.

timeline.e: Terraform plans to create many resources that already exist because the state file is missing.
The agent is asked to clean up duplicates; an older state file is placed on the new machine.
terraform destroy removes the VPC, RDS database, ECS cluster, load balancers and bastion host.
Automated snapshots also appear to be gone; the author upgrades to AWS Business Support.
AWS engineers confirm the deletion and find a snapshot not visible in the console.
The database is restored and back online, about 24 hours after the deletion.

rootCause.trigger: The Terraform state file was not on the new machine, then an older state was used, and a destroy ran against production.
rootCause.underlying: An AI agent was allowed to run Terraform commands without review.
contributing: Two projects shared one configuration and VPC
Snapshots were tied to the database and deleted with it
No deletion protection or remote state

diagnose.step: Check Terraform state location and version.
Review the plan before apply or destroy.

correct.step: Stop the agent from running destructive commands.

prevent.step: Keep state in remote versioned storage.
Require manual approval for destructive actions.

fix.safety: Never let an agent run apply or destroy on production without a human reading the plan.

troubleshoot.scenario: Terraform proposes creating everything because the state file is missing. An agent offers to clean up and destroy duplicates.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
troubleshoot.answer: Stop, find the right state, never destroy on production without review, enable protection and keep backups outside the stack.

rootcause.q: What went missing that caused Terraform to plan everything again?

design.prompt: Design infrastructure automation safe from accidental destroy.
design.answer: Remote state, locks, deletion protection, separate backups, scoped credentials and review.
